title: git diff shows nothing — because you staged it
summary: There are three snapshots in play and diff compares two of them at a time. Learn which pair each form of the command uses, and the confusion disappears permanently.
mental_model: `git diff` = working tree vs index. `git diff --staged` = index vs HEAD. `git diff HEAD` = working tree vs HEAD. Three snapshots, three comparisons, and the default is the one people forget.

steps.title: Change two files, stage one
steps.why: This sets up the state where all three diffs differ. pump.py will be staged; sensor.py will be left in the working tree only.
steps.expect: M  pump.py (staged) and  M sensor.py (not staged) — note which column the M sits in.

steps.title: The default diff, and why it looks incomplete
steps.why: Bare `git diff` compares the working tree with the index. pump.py is identical in both — you already staged it — so it does not appear. This is the moment people conclude git has eaten their change.
steps.expect: Only sensor.py. pump.py is invisible here.

steps.title: The staged diff — what your next commit will contain
steps.why: `--staged` (or `--cached`, same thing) compares the index with HEAD. This is the true preview of your commit, and worth running every single time before you commit.
steps.expect: Only pump.py, with both lines changed.

steps.title: Everything since the last commit
steps.why: `git diff HEAD` compares the working tree with HEAD, ignoring the index entirely. It is the answer to 'what have I done since my last commit', regardless of what is staged.

steps.title: Commit and confirm what got in
steps.why: Only the staged change is committed. sensor.py stays modified in the working tree, exactly as the three diffs predicted.
commands: git commit -m "Ramp the pump to 1600 RPM"

verify.label: sensor.py was not — it was never staged

steps.title: Diffs worth knowing beyond the three
steps.why: `--stat` for shape, `--word-diff` for prose and config files, `-w` to ignore whitespace churn, and `--name-only` for scripting. These four cover most real review work.

verify.label: the unstaged file stayed out of the commit
sensor.py is still modified in the working tree
verify.hint: leave it unstaged — that is the point of the scenario

verify.label: nothing is staged any more, because the commit consumed it

pitfalls: `git diff` after staging everything shows nothing at all. That is correct behaviour, not a lost change.
`git diff branch1 branch2` compares tips; `git diff branch1...branch2` compares against the merge base. Code review tools use the three-dot form.
`git diff` pages by default in a normal terminal. `--no-pager` or `| cat` in scripts.
cheatsheet: working tree vs index — what is NOT staged
index vs HEAD — what your commit WILL contain
working tree vs HEAD — everything since the last commit
files and line counts instead of full hunks
changes on b since it diverged from a
